comments.text:
Gum arabic, or acacia gum, is a natural, edible gum from acacia trees used in food as a stabilizer, emulsifier, and thickener in products like soft drinks, candies, and icings, preventing sugar crystallization and fat separation. It's a soluble dietary fiber that's generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA, acting as a binder and texturizer in many confections, baked goods, and beverages, and is also used in non-food items like watercolor paints and stamp adhesiv

Xanthan gum is a common food additive and plant-based powder used to thicken, stabilize, and bind ingredients in cooking, baking, and industrial products. It is made when sugar is fermented by a bacteria named Xanthomonas campestris, then dried and milled.

Maltodextrin is a highly processed, water-soluble white powder made from plant starches like corn, rice, potato, or wheat. It serves as a common food additive to thicken products, improve texture, and extend shelf life. It provides 4 calories per gram.

Everyone wondering what the ingredients are xD you are all dumb.

Lastly silica: Human bodies do not break down silica (silicon dioxide). Because silica is chemically inert and insoluble in digestive fluids, it passes right through your digestive tract unchanged. A tiny amount dissolves into liquid as silicic acid and enters the blood to leave via urine, but solid silica stays intact

Just because you dont know what it is, and it sounds like a weird word, makes it seem like its a bad thing. Most of these are just alertnative to flour or corn starch.
